newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Regal Int to focus on China infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: Regal Int to focus on China infrastructure.

text.p: Regal International Inc plans to turn itself into a China infrastructure play and seek a listing on a major U.S. stock exchange, president Mico Chung said on Thursday.
Regal, a 49.5 percent associate of China Strategic Holdings Ltd, is currently listed on the Nasdaq bulletin board in the United States.
"We are now building Regal into a corporation suitable for listing on a major stock exchange in the U.S.," said Chung.

The company agreed to issue US$30 million worth of convertible notes to China Strategic for its 51 percent interest in Hangzhou Zhongche Huantong Development Co Ltd, which is involved in building and operating a toll road at Hangzhou, in China's Zhejiang province.
China Strategic intends to convert a substantial part of the note into new Regal shares in due couse, the firm said.
Regal also disposed of its 55 percent equity interest in Wuxi CSI Vibration Isolator Co Ltd for US$13.95 million in cash.
Chung said in a statement it was the right time to reorganise Regal into a major infrastructure play corporation in China, where there were better opportunities for growth.

Hangzhou Zhongche, a Sino-foreign joint venture formed in 1993, is building the 38.2-km long Hangzhou Ring Road, with the final phase to be completed by the end of 1997 and traffic to start in early 1998, he said.
Toll revenues from the completed sections of the road reached 37.2 million yuan in 1995.
Regal currently engages in manufacturing and distribution of oil exploration, drilling and recovery equipment in the United States. -- Hong Kong News Room (852) 2843 6369
